newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes end up as paper dumped in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes end up as paper dumped in late trade.

text.p: Late selling extended early gains in Mexican overnight Cetes rates MXAAB, closing 100 basis points higher at 23 percent, traders said.

"Rates were again forced up towards the close by traders who dumped paper to obtain liquidity, after hanging on to it in the hope of selling at lower rates. The average for today's session was 22.50 percent," a trader said.
"It was a very quiet session. Traders are preferring to wait and see what happens at tomorrow's primary auction, so there won't be much trade for now," he added.
Traders expected the benchmark 28-day Cetes rate to gain slightly from last week's rate of 23.38 percent at Tuesday's auction.
Liquidity pressures during the session were eased by government spending of 1.4 billion pesos, traders said.
Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, closed up 30 basis points at 24.30 percent.
Total credit maturities for Tuesday were estimated at 5.557 billion pesos.
